full_judgment:
5. Mr. Asrarul Hossain, the learned' Advocate appearing for the plaintiff appellant, has contended that the Commercial Court has erred (1) firstly, in not awarding interest to the plaintiff bank on the decretal amount from the date of institution of the suit to the date of the decree or the interest pendente lite contrary to Order 34 rules 2, 7 and 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure and (2) secondly, in not awarding interest to the plaintiff on the decretal amount from the date of the decree to the date of realisation of the same. He has lastly contended that in view of the fact that the Commercial Court has not allowed any interest to the plaintiff on the decretal amount the Commercial Court has erred in allowing longer instalments to the defendants for payment of the decretal amount In support of his contentions the learned Advocate has referred us the cases of Dawoodbhai Kassemji Matiwalla and another Vs. Shaikhalibhoy, AIR 1953 (Bom) 445 and Kishenlal and others Vs. Radhalal and others AIR 1958 (Rajasthan) 145. 

 6. In reply Mr. Golam Rabbani, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondents, has contended that the instant suit is not a suit for foreclosure, redemption or for promissory note and as such the cases reported in AIR 1953 (Bom) 445 and in AIR 1958 (Rajasthan) 145 have no application in the instant case. He has next contended that the Commercial Court has given valid reasons for disallowing the interest and therefore its decision disallowing the interest to the plaintiff is not liable to be interfered with. 

 8. In the case in AIR 1958 Rajasthan 145 the plaintiffs brought the suit for redemption of mortgage on payment of a sum of Rs. 3400/- to the defendants and a question of payment of interest arose. In these circumstances a single Bench of Rajasthan High Court held: 

 The instant suit was not brought for redemption of mortgage but in AIR 1958 Rajasthan 145 the suit was brought for redemption of mortgage and as such the case in AIR 1958 Rajasthan 145 has no application in the instant case. Rules 2 and 11 of Order 34 of the Code of Civil Procedure refer to suit for preclosure of mortgage and Rule 7 of Order 34 refers to a suit for redemption of mortgage and as such Rules 2, 7 and 11 of Order 34 of the Civil Procedure Code are not attracted in the instant case. Moreover, the cases in AIR 1953 (Bom) 445 and in AIR 1958 Rajsthan145 refer to interest on mortgage money but that is not so in the instant case. It was not laid down in the said two cases that the plaintiffs were entitled to interest on decretal amount as a matter of right or that the payment of interest on decretal amount was compulsory and if considered from this angle also the said two cases have no application in the instant case.
